title: Token hedging, KV coherence, and graceful fallback playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a lightweight playbook for integrating speculative (opportunistic) token-ahead decoding into the serving runtime while keeping KV-cache coherence across model variants and providing clear acceptance, rollback, and telemetry. The doc attempts to bridge kernel routing, scheduler priorities, and KV-cache reconciliation so rollout engineers can experiment safely and revert without data correctness or performance regressions.

Audience:
- Serving runtime owners
- Model onboarding engineers
- SREs running Dedicated/Private clusters
- Product/QA for rollout acceptance

Background and motivation:
Speculative decoding (we call it token hedging in this doc) can reduce tail latency by starting ahead for tokens we predict will be needed. However, starting speculative work introduces KV-cache divergence, increased compute pressure, and complex interactions with kernel selection (quantized path vs full-precision). We need a pragmatic integration plan that: 1) keeps correctness for served streams, 2) ensures graceful degradation/backout, and 3) provides observability for model rollouts and performance regressions.

High-level design principles:
- Non-invasive defaults: token hedging must be off by default for new models unless explicitly enabled via rollout policy.
- Deterministic reconciliation: whenever speculative outputs are made visible, the system ensures the final token stream is from the canonical (non-speculative or validated) path.
- Localized risk: prefetch/speculative tasks should be tagged and schedulable on lower-priority backfill lanes; no speculative task should evict critical KV state for high-priority requests.
- Telemetry-first: define a minimal set of metrics and traces that will quickly reveal regressions in latency, cost, or correctness.

Components and responsibilities:
1) Kernel router
- Inputs: model config (quantization level, kernel family), request SLO, sequence length estimate, speculative_enabled flag.
- Behavior: choose kernel variant for canonical and speculative runs. For example, speculative tasks prefer a faster/fewer-precision kernel (e.g., int8 with fused attention) to minimize cost; canonical path uses the verified kernel.
- Interface: the router exposes a SelectorKey string that downstream components can use for compatibility checks (e.g., "gpt2-xl|int8|fast-attn").

2) Scheduler and lanes
- Lanes: realtime (high priority), speculative (low priority), background-evict (maintenance).
- Policy: scheduler caps speculative concurrency per GPU to a fraction (configurable, default 20%) of realtime capacity to prevent noisy-neighbor effects.
- Preemption: realtime tasks can preempt speculative lanes; preemption triggers a KV reconciliation step for the preempted speculative slots.

3) KV-cache manager and coherence model
- KV fragment tagging: every KV write is annotated with request_id, speculative_tag (true/false), and kernel_selector.
- Coherence rules:
  - Reads for canonical requests ignore speculative-tagged fragments unless a reconciliation commit has occurred.
  - When a speculative result is validated (see validation flow), the speculative fragments are promoted (tag removed) and merged into the canonical cache using a deterministic merge order (request timestamp, token index).
  - Eviction constraints: eviction must consider frag tags; speculative fragments are first-class but low-priority for retention.

4) Validation and commit flow
- Local validation: speculative outputs are cross-checked against a cheap consistency check (e.g., top-K token set overlap, checksum of KV snapshot) before commit.
- Remote/verified validation: for aggressive rollouts, we may run an N=2 canonical run in a cold path to compare outputs; if mismatch exceeds thresholds, do not commit speculative KV.

Acceptance criteria (for model onboarding with token hedging enabled):
- Latency: p95 must improve by >= 5% vs baseline with no more than 3% p50 regression.
- Correctness: end-to-end generation divergence (edit distance normalized) between canonical and served output <= 0.5% on curated prompt set; mismatches must be logged and sampled.
- Cost: per-token GPU cycles should not exceed baseline by more than 10% (configurable).
- Stability: no increase in error rate (OOMs, kernel faults) above 0.1% of requests.
- Observability: rollout must surface the metrics listed below and provide tracing linking speculative tokens to kernel_selector and KV fragment ids.

Rollback triggers and playbook:
- Automatic triggers (able to auto-failover within rollout window):
  - Latency regressions: p95 increases by > 15% sustained over 5 minutes.
  - Correctness regression: divergence > 2% on production prompt sampler for 10k requests.
  - Resource exhaustion: speculative lanes cause GPU memory pressure resulting in >0.2% OOMs.
- Manual triggers: unusual error patterns, customer reports of hallucinations correlated with rollout window.
- Rollback steps (fast path):
  1) Flip rollout flag to disable speculative flag for the model (config push).
  2) Drain speculative lane: stop accepting new speculative tasks, let in-flight speculative tasks complete (with timeout).
  3) Reconcile cache: invalidate speculative KV fragments (or demote them) for all active shards.
  4) Verify baseline: run smoke canonical queries against canonical kernel.
  5) Communicate: post incident note to rollout channel and update JIRA rollout ticket.

Telemetry (minimal required metrics and traces):
- spec.decoding.enabled (gauge per model variant)
- spec.decoding.started (counter)
- spec.decoding.committed (counter)
- spec.decoding.rejected (counter with reason tags: validation_mismatch, resource_pressure, preempted)
- spec.kv.fragments.created (counter)
- spec.kv.fragments.promoted (counter)
- spec.kv.fragments.evicted (counter)
- spec.kernel.selection (histogram of kernel_selector usage)
- spec.latency.delta_ms (histogram of difference between canonical p95 and served p95 when speculative was active)
- spec.cost.delta_cycles (gauge sample)
- Traces: for each request where speculative is used, include span tags: request_id, speculative_tag, kernel_selector, kv_fragment_ids (list string), validation_result.

Experiment plan and canary strategy:
- Stage 1 (internal canary): enable per-model token hedging at 1% of traffic on dedicated test clusters with synthetic prompt set; require acceptance metrics above.
- Stage 2 (customer beta): Scoped by customer opt-in; collect production telemetry for 48 hours.
- Stage 3 (regional rollout): Ramp 10 -> 25 -> 50% with automated rollback gates.

Compatibility checks and pre-ons:
- Model compatibility script: must validate model architecture, KV shape expectations, and kernel availability. Failure blocks speculative flag.
- Kernel compatibility: if speculative kernel lacks exact operator parity, speculative must run with conservative constraints (no promotion to canonical cache unless validated).

Operational runbook snippets:
- If GPU memory pressure observed with speculative on: reduce per-GPU speculative concurrency to 10% and increase prefetch token threshold.
- If validation_mismatch spike: pause rollout immediately, collect example IDs, run diffs with canonical path locally, escalate to model leads.
- If fragments.evicted increases sharply: increase speculative eviction TTL and consider increasing background-evict capacity window.

Checklist for model onboarding (quick):
- [ ] Model passes compatibility script (kernel/operator checks)
- [ ] Baseline perf profiles collected (p50/p95 cost and latency)
- [ ] Curated prompt set for divergence checks uploaded to model artifact
- [ ] Telemetry instrumentation verified on staging
- [ ] Rollout config prepared with automatic rollback thresholds

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle multi-tenant KV shards if speculative fragments are committed from lower-priority lanes? (risk: noisy neighbor influencing other tenants)
- Cost transparency: speculative CPU/GPU cycles must be billed separately or attributed to tenant in Dedicated; pricing model TBD.
- Side-channel correctness: parity checks must be cheap; designing a good cheap-local validation is nontrivial.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Jordan: prototype kernel_selector tagging in router and expose selector in traces (two-week spike).
- Priya: implement speculative fragment tagging and demotion in KV manager (one-week spike).
- Samir: add telemetry counters and dashboards (staging, then prod).
- Maya: run first internal canary on test cluster and collect baseline.

Appendix: useful links
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infer/pull/1234
- Rollout ticket: JIRA-ENG-9876
- Slack discussion: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345/p1640000000

Notes: keep this doc as the minimal playbook — for long-form design/spec we will extract kernel routing pseudocode and KV API changes into a separate spec once the prototype stabilizes.
